explanation: This expert-level C++ concept explores compile-time polymorphism achieved through `constexpr` functions and template metaprogramming.  It delves into how the compiler generates highly optimized code by evaluating function calls and template instantiations at compile time, eliminating runtime overhead.  We'll examine the memory layout implications, focusing on how the compiler avoids runtime function calls and memory allocations by generating specialized code for different template arguments.  We'll also touch on the potential for increased compile times and code size when dealing with complex metaprograms.
